entries.noteEn: Recommended neither candidate; preferred a broad Labor–Likud government. Two independent contemporary reports; the President’s House minute was not recovered.

cites.quote: The decision gave Shamir the support of 63 members of Israel's 120-member parliament, the Knesset. Foreign Minister Shimon Peres, leader of the center-left Labor Party and Shamir's rival in the current governing coalition, could muster only 55 Knesset members to support a Labor-led government.

Of the two other religious parties, one of them, the National Religious Party, pledged its five seats to Likud last week. The other, Degel Hatorah, pledged its two Knesset seats to a broad-based coalition of Labor and Likud.

The leftist Mapam and Citizens Rights Movement, as well as the Center-Shinui Movement, have declared their preference for a Labor-led government. They urged Herzog to approach Foreign Minister Shimon Peres. The right-wing Tehiya, Tsomet and Moledet parties all have opted for a Likud government headed by Premier Yitzhak Shamir.

With its own 40 seats and the 11 seats offered Sunday, plus previously pledged support from one other religious party and three far-right parties, Likud can claim a majority with 63 seats in the 120-member Knesset

notes: Contemporary reporting gives aggregate support of 63 for Shamir and 55 for Peres; that agreement is a consistency check, not evidence of any single list. JTA (9 November) names the non-Arab parties’ choices. Hadash, PLP and ADP rest on one retrospective account (Local Call, 2022); Degel HaTorah on l’Unità (14 November 1988) and UPI.

7 November policy pass (docs/source-policy.md): Degel is none (probable: l’Unità 14 November 1988 and UPI, independent contemporary reports). Hadash, PLP and ADP recommended Peres conditionally (provisional: one retrospective, Local Call 2022). The President’s House consultation file for 7–13 November 1988 remains the deciding record. The totals now match the contemporary 63–55 report; that agreement is a consistency check, not evidence.
